questions.q: How had Solomon improved the place where Yahweh would live?
questions.a: Yahweh had said he would live in thick darkness, but Solomon built him a lofty residence in which he would live forever.

questions.q: Where did Yahweh finally decide to live and whom did he chose to rule over Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh had chosen no city in which to build his house nor any man to be prince over Israel, but he then chose Jerusalem as the city and David to be over Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say to David to keep him from fulfilling the desire of his heart?
questions.a: Yahweh had told David, “It was in your heart to build a house for my name, but your son will build it instead.”

questions.q: How did Yahweh carry out the word that he had spoken?
questions.a: Yahweh carried out the word he had spoken by having Solomon sit on David’s throne, build the house for the name of Yahweh, and place the ark within it.

questions.q: How did Solomon stand before the altar of Yahweh?
questions.a: Solomon stood on a bronze platform, knelt down before all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward the heavens.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do for the servants who walk before him with all their heart?
questions.a: Yahweh keeps covenant and covenant faithfulness with his servants who walk before him with all their heart.

questions.q: What is the promise which Yahweh made to his servant David?
questions.a: Yahweh told David that he would not fail to have a man from his tribe sit on the throne of Israel if his descendants were careful to walk in Yahweh’s law.

questions.q: What was the basic request which Solomon made of Yahweh?
questions.a: Solomon requested that Yahweh listen to his cry and prayer so that his eyes would be open on the temple day and night.

questions.q: What did Solomon want Yahweh, the God of Israel, to do after Yahweh listened to the requests of Solomon and the people of Israel?
How could a righteous man be declared innocent if he was charged with sinning against his neighbor?
questions.a: A righteous man could be declared innocent by swearing an oath before the altar in Yahweh’s house.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel need to do when they had been defeated by an enemy because they had sinned against Yahweh?
questions.a: The people of Israel needed to turn back to Yahweh by confessing his name, praying, and requesting forgiveness before him in the temple.

questions.q: How should the people of Israel respond when the skies are shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against Yahweh?
questions.a: The people of Israel should pray toward the temple, confess Yahweh’s name, and turn from their sin so that rain would fall on their land.

questions.q: What were some of the conditions where people in Israel needed Yahweh to listen to their prayers and forgive them for their sins?
questions.a: The people in Israel needed Yahweh to listen to their prayers when there was famine, disease, blight or mildew, locusts or caterpillars, when enemies attacked the city gates, or if there was any plague or sickness.

questions.q: Why should Yahweh do what the foreigner asks of him when he came and prayed toward Yahweh’s house?
questions.a: Yahweh should do what the foreigner asked of him so that all the people groups on earth might know Yahweh’s name, fear him, and know the house which is called by his name.

questions.q: What request did Solomon make of Yahweh?
questions.a: Solomon requested that Yahweh would listen to the confession of the people of Israel and forgive them of their sins after they had sinned, been taken captive to the land of their enemy, and repented of their sins.

questions.q: What did Solomon want Yahweh to do?
questions.a: Solomon wanted Yahweh to be attentive to the prayers of the people, clothe his priests with salvation, and let his saints rejoice in his goodness.

commentary.text: Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple.

—The order of Solomon's prayer is to be observed. First and chiefly, he prays for repentance and forgiveness, which is the chief blessing, and the only solid foundation of other mercies: he then prays for temporal mercies; thereby teaching us what things to mind and desire most in our prayers. This also Christ hath taught us in his perfect pattern and form of prayer, where there is but one prayer for outward, and all the rest are for spiritual blessings. The temple typified the human nature of Christ, in whom dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. The ark typified his obedience and sufferings, by which repenting sinners have access to a reconciled God, and communion with him. Jehovah has made our nature his resting-place for ever, in the person of Emmanuel, and through him he dwells with, and delights in his church of redeemed sinners. May our hearts become his resting-place; may Christ dwell therein by faith, consecrating them as his temples, and shedding abroad his love therein. May the Father look upon us in and through his Anointed; and may he remember and bless us in all things, according to his mercy to sinners, in and through Christ.
